PC: Assess the situation by gaining information from the bystander
Gathers essential and accurate information from bystander (history of present illness, initial vital signs in the field, symptoms, severity, duration).
Sequences critical actions in patient care: ABCs, vital signs, other therapeutic interventions.
Reevaluates patient after stabilization, and following interventions.
Perform a timely and appropriate secondary survey
Recognize and treat hypovolemia secondary to hemorrhage
Demonstrate the correct sequence of steps to apply a tourniquet
Reassess casualty if there are any changes or after the casualty is moved
MK: Determine medical need and required intervention
Describes an appropriate differential, plan, and disposition.
Explains the pathologic basis for management.
SBP: Can handle distractions while maintaining patient care priorities.
Initiate a timely request for evacuation
ICS: The learner introduces himself/herself to the suspect, properly or the suspect hangs up, and then the bystander who will provide the care
Communicate proper steps of intervention using lay-terms in a timely manner to save patient’s life
Update negotiator/commander of the patient’s condition
Introduces self and efficiently establishes respectful and effective communication with bystander/suspect.
Communicates clearly, concisely, and professionally with all involved regarding patient status and interventions.
